text: It's less a hard canon fact and a bit more of extrapolation, but Koishi has what feels like the biggest evidence of that Spell Card rules aren't as foolproof as the community likes to paint them and that you probably can loophole abuse. Release of Id and Superego are very similar in structure and it's extra notorious because they're almost back to back, only separated by a non-spell. They shoot heart-shaped danmaku in sort of constantly rotating parabolic trajectories with the individual lanes criss-crossing. The main difference being that former is shot outwards (and gameplay-wise has hearts pile up at the bottom of screen), while the latter "falls" inwards (and has the hearts disappear when they reach their target). Even Twilight Frontier seems to have noticed; when she's playable in the air fighters they're still separate supers, but her story appearance in Hopeless Masquerade just merges them into one Spell Card that alternates between the two patterns. Ref, give her a yellow card, girl put more effort into re-using the structure of Rorschach in Danmaku for Genetics of the Unconscious than whatever the hell is happening here. There's even a break with dick danmaku Embers of Love in-between. It also doesn't really help that some of Marisa's comments in Grimoire of Marisa boil down to something like "yeah good luck dealing with this one".
